title: ConcurrentHashMap in JDK 7 versus JDK 8
context: How does ConcurrentHashMap in JDK 8 differ from JDK 7?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: JDK 7 split the map into a fixed number of segments, each a ReentrantLock-protected HashMap, so concurrency was limited to that many threads. JDK 8 removed segments. It locks individual bins with synchronized and uses CAS for empty bins, which gives finer locking and better throughput. JDK 8 also uses trees for long bins, which the segment design did not.

points.title: Segments removed
points.why: JDK 7 capped concurrent writers at the segment count. JDK 8 locks bins instead.

points.title: Better behaviour under collisions
points.why: Trees in JDK 8 limit lookup cost in long bins.
